- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) in recent days, increase forecast downward bias to reflect bearish momentum.  
- When model shows steep upward trend after a spike, cap forecast growth to prevent overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows sharp reversal from high, model should adjust downward faster than linear trend.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if history shows mean reversion (e.g., recent prices oscillating around 80–85), model should not assume sustained trend.  
- If sentiment is neutral or low (0.0–0.3) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast magnitude to avoid false momentum.  
- If true outcome is significantly below forecast (e.g., >10% gap), check if sentiment was bullish recently — if so, adjust downward by 5–10% to reflect sentiment misalignment.
